a.onclick: openModal( this, "Intracellular Enzyme", ["36678793"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36678793/"], ["In the context of protein replacement therapy - intracellular enzymes or other cytosolic proteins, the simplest design is a non‑secreted ORF lacking signal peptides or transmembrane segments so that translation occurs on free ribosomes and the protein remains in the cytosol or nucleus. If organelle targeting is needed (mitochondria, peroxisomes, nucleus), the mRNA must encode the corresponding localization signals such as Mitochondrial Targeting Sequence (MTS) or Nuclear Localization Signal (NLS) at the protein level"])

openModal( this, "Proteins can be Secreted through the Golgi Apparatus", ["30885573"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30885573/"], ["For secreted proteins, such as antibodies, the mRNA ORF typically begins with an N‑terminal signal peptide that directs the nascent chain into the ER lumen, where the signal peptide is cleaved, the protein folds and is glycosylated, and then travels through the Golgi for vesicular secretion. By grafting signal peptides from known secreted proteins, mRNA constructs can turn transfected cells into “protein factories” that release therapeutic enzymes, cytokines, or antibodies into the circulation"])

openModal( this, "Degradation Competes with Translation", ["35597779"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35597779/"], ["After endosomal escape, therapeutic mRNAs join the same pool as endogenous transcripts and are partitioned between translation on ribosomes and decay by the cellular mRNA turnover machinery. Most endogenous mRNAs are first deadenylated and then degraded, and these pathways also act on exogenous mRNAs"])

openModal( this, "mRNA does not integrate into the genome", ["34433919"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34433919/"], ["One important safety advantage of mRNA‑based therapies is that mRNA remains in the cytoplasm and is translated by ribosomes without entering the nucleus, so it does not integrate into the host genome"])

openModal( this, "Cells endocyte LNPs via different routes", ["33666625"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33666625/"], ["Once LNPs reach the target tissue, they can be uptaken via different routes, depending on their formulation - and protein corona -functionalization, but also on cell type"])

openModal( this, "Therapeutic mRNA is a “Plug‑and‑Play” Template that Hijacks the Host’s Own Translation Apparatus", ["35597779","20094052"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35597779/","https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20094052/"], ["Therapeutic mRNAs are translated entirely by the host’s endogenous machinery, using the same ribosomes, initiation factors, and tRNAs that normally decode cellular transcripts","The 5′ cap structure and 3′ poly(A) tail of synthetic mRNAs recruit cap‑binding complexes (eIF4E/eIF4G/eIF4A) and poly(A)‑binding protein, which circularize the mRNA and promote efficient translation initiation in a manner analogous to endogenous cap‑dependent mRNAs"])

openModal( this, "Endocytosed LNPs converge in the endo-lysosomal network", ["38437552"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38437552/"], ["Regardless of the pathway of uptake, LNPs all end up in early endosomes: the first compartment where the internalized payload resides once it has been endocytosed by a cell. Endosomes are highly dynamic organelles and they carry out the trafficking of the mRNA-LNP therapeutic"])

openModal( this, "Endosomal Escape is a Rare Event", ["38437552","40595685"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38437552/","https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40595685/"], ["For mRNA to be translated, it needs to escape the endosomal compartment and reach the cytoplasm. This escape is considered a bottleneck, since only 1%-10% of mRNAs manage to escape the endosome. Escape is not the norm, but a rare event that happens at a specific level of endosomal acidification. The acid environment protonates the ionizable lipids, leading to damages to the membrane and release of the cargo","There are different approaches to study and quantify escape events, with different levels of detail and complexity. Importantly, escape has been studied lengthy for siRNA therapeutics, but newer results show how siRNA and mRNA behave differently inside the endosomes: mRNA is a world on its own!"])

openModal( this, "Different Delivery Routes are possible", ["26264835","36351374"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26264835/","https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36351374/"], ["Generally, the delivery route determines the bioavailability of a drug. In the context of mRNA-based therapy, the delivery route (intravenous, intramuscular, intradermal, inhalation, etc.) should be chosen to maximize the delivery to the target tissue. Thus, the route depends on the properties of the LNP and on the disease indication.","mRNA vaccines (e.g. SARS‑CoV‑2) are delivered in muscle and the transfected cell population consists of infiltrating monocytes/DCs, while mRNA therapies for protein replacement are often delivered intravenously, with LNPs designed to reach the desired tissue."])

openModal( this, "Membrane Proteins", ["39687732"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39687732/"], ["Membrane proteins, such as membrane-bound antigens, require one or more signal sequences and transmembrane domains in the encoded polypeptide so that, after translation on ER‑bound ribosomes, they are inserted into the ER membrane and then trafficked to the plasma membrane or internal organelles via the secretory pathway"])

openModal( this, "Antigen Presentation", ["29326426"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29326426/"], ["For antigens, the mRNA can be engineered so that the encoded antigen is optimized for MHC class I and/or class II loading, for example by targeting expression to dendritic cells, adding secretion signals, or fusing antigens to trafficking or membrane‑anchoring domains that enhance processing. mRNA vaccines often encode full‑length or membrane‑anchored viral proteins, or antigens fused to MHC‑related domains, that markedly increase cross‑presentation and CD8⁺ T‑cell priming compared to cytosolic antigens alone"])

openModal( this, "Protein Corona Defines the Biological Identity", ["38757190"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38757190/"], ["After PEG shedding, the lipid surface is exposed to a variety of different plasma proteins, forming the protein corona. It defines the biological identity of the nanoparticle and it influences cellular internalization"])

openModal( this, "The Nascent Peptide Chain needs Further Processing", ["8696972"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8696972/"], ["As the nascent peptide emerges from the ribosome exit tunnel, it begins to fold co‑translationally, first forming local secondary structures and then compacting into higher‑order domains as more of the chain appears, with the help of chaperons such as the Hsp70 systems. Once fully synthesized and released, the polypeptide can further mature with the help of cytosolic chaperones (Hsp70s, chaperonins)"])

openModal( this, "Degradation can happen co-translationally", ["24091060"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24091060/"], ["Translation and decay are tightly interconnected processes: efficient translation initiation and elongation can stabilize transcripts, whereas impaired initiation or ribosome run‑off exposes mRNAs to degradation, even when translation is still occurring"])

openModal( this, "The Dynamic State of Proteins", ["35305310"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35305310/"], ["After synthesis and initial folding, many proteins are continuously surveyed, and those that are misfolded, damaged, or no longer needed are selectively removed by two main degradation systems: the proteasome and lysosomes, both depending on ubiquitination"])

openModal( this, "PEG Lipids are Molecular Timers", ["34433919","24345865"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34433919/","https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24345865/"], ["Functionalized PEG-lipids provide a transient hydrophilic shield that reduces aggregation and opsonization, but they also act as molecular “timers”: their shedding kinetics, regulated by lipid anchor length, expose the underlying lipid surface to plasma proteins","Noticeably, even small variations in PEG structure, like varying anchor length (10-18 carbons), or in molar fraction, yield markedly different LNP half life in vivo"])

openModal( this, "Correct Protein Localization is determined by Signal Peptides", ["40563537"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40563537/"], ["Signal peptides (SPs) are short N-terminal sequences (typically 16-30 amino acids) that guide nascent proteins to their correct cellular destinations. There are several transport pathways that leverage the SPs and can act co- or post-translationally. The use of SPs is pivotal in mRNA-based therapeutics, with the majority of vaccines now incorporating the tissue plasminogen activator SP."])

openModal( this, "mRNAs localize in cellular subcompartments", ["25549890"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25549890/"], ["Localization elements are nucleotide sequences on the 3’ UTR that operate like subcellular localization ‘zip codes’. These ‘zip codes’ are recognized by RNA-binding proteins (RBPs), which in turn mediate the binding to motors and adaptor proteins, directing the mRNA where translation occurs. This ensures that newly synthesized proteins reach their correct membrane, secretory, or cytosolic destination."])
